response.sql: SELECT language_id, AVG(replacement_cost) AS avg_replacement_cost, AVG(length) AS avg_length FROM film WHERE length >= 112 GROUP BY language_id ORDER BY AVG(length) IS NULL, AVG(length) DESC LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: The database is MySQL, matching the schema's syntax, so the NULLS LAST ordering is written as ORDER BY AVG(length) IS NULL, AVG(length) DESC.
The length filter is inclusive (length >= 112) and drops films with NULL length before grouping, so each group's average running time is never NULL. The NULL-last ordering is kept as a safeguard.
Grouping uses film.language_id as the request states, not original_language_id. replacement_cost is NOT NULL, so AVG ignores no values for it.
